Restored mangroves sequester more carbon than unvegetated tidal flats [ev_carbon_sequestration_su21_1], sustainable forest management sites under GEF projects sequester about 1.33 t of carbon per hectare per year more than the counterfactual [ev_carbon_sequestration_gefieo19_1], and secondary regrowth in the central Amazon of Brazil reached 50% of mature forest biomass after 25 years [ev_carbon_sequestration_gehring05_1].
conditionality: Biomass recovery is slow (about 12 decades to reach 90% of old-growth above-ground biomass) even though topsoil carbon recovers in about 5 years [ev_carbon_sequestration_poorter21_1, ev_soil_organic_carbon_poorter21_1]. Afforestation soil carbon gains were not significant on pastures and grasslands and boreal sites lost 1.5% [ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_2, ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_4], community management in Madagascar did not halt clearing [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_1], the modelled estimates are discounted present values or scenario potentials, and planted-forest removal factors include commercial woodlots. Soil carbon and forest cover enter as component proxies, and the low-income evidence is mostly compiler ratings.

effect_mechanism: Planting native trees on former pasture in Brazil's Atlantic Forest built up carbon stocks of 21.85, 25.78 and 38.29 Mg/ha in successively older plantings, against 138.94 Mg/ha in mature forest [ev_carbon_sequestration_azevedo18_1, ev_carbon_sequestration_azevedo18_3]; a global review puts removal rates for planted forests and woodlots at 4.5 to 40.7 t CO2/ha/yr over the first 20 years [ev_carbon_sequestration_bernal18_1]. A systematic review found that flooding or peak flows decreased with forest cover expansion in 82% of studies reporting them [ev_flood_hazard_filoso17_1]. WOCAT compilers for area closures in Ethiopia, afforestation in Eritrea, Cabo Verde, Uganda and Bosnia and Herzegovina, floodplain reafforestation in Tajikistan, mangrove buffers in the Philippines, mangrove afforestation in Bangladesh and a learning site in Afghanistan rate downstream flooding or flood impacts as reduced; an Ethiopian compiler notes that runoff from the watershed is highly reduced, and the Afghan compiler that riverbanks were revegetated with communities planting cuttings along banks and shorelines [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1072_2011_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1048_2011_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1330_2010_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1509_2011_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_578_2016_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_4300_2019_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7460_2024_flood_impacts].

The Honduras compiler rates no downstream change yet, expecting reforestation to reduce floods in the lower river only in the long term, and the Bangladesh and Bosnia and Herzegovina compilers rate only a slight reduction [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_750_2016_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_4300_2019_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_4367_2019_downstream_flooding]. effect_mechanism: Mangrove belts lower coastal flood impact by attenuating wind waves and, far more weakly, storm-surge water levels as water passes through the forest, with attenuation depending on inundation depth, tree species, density and creeks. A global flood model finds that losing current mangroves would increase the land, people and property flooded each year, and in Orissa, India, villages behind mangroves had fewer cyclone deaths and lower household losses; WOCAT compilers in Bangladesh and the Philippines rate flood impacts as decreased. In Bangladesh, a cited model finds 500 m mangrove afforestation patches can mitigate surge current velocities by up to 90% [ev_flood_hazard_wbmang25_2].
conditionality: Almost all measured and modelled evidence concerns existing mangrove forests rather than restored stands, so the transfer to restoration is assumed. Measured surge reductions come from south Florida in the USA, wave reductions are upper bounds partly derived from small-wave measurements, and the Orissa household-loss comparison is a perception-based survey of a few villages. The Bangladesh study is modelled grey literature from the World Bank, and it finds mangroves have only a small effect (<4%) on design total water level because the surge dominates, so their benefit there is protection of embankments from erosion and currents rather than lower flood levels [ev_flood_hazard_wbmang25_1, ev_flood_hazard_wbmang25_2].

effect_mechanism: Across restoration families the gain runs mostly through fodder and livestock: WOCAT compilers in Ethiopia, Eritrea, Tanzania, Tunisia, Niger, India, Cape Verde, Turkmenistan and Afghanistan rate fodder and animal production as increased, from cut-and-carry grass in enclosures, planted sand-fixing species used as forage and better grazing management. Crop gains are reported where regeneration improves soils or supplies mulch, and in Niger assisted natural regeneration in fields is reported to raise millet and sorghum output by almost 50%; in Brazil the Reflorestar payments-for-ecosystem-services programme raised agricultural value added and production value in the poorest municipalities. In Tigray, Ethiopia, households downstream of exclosures harvested 188 to 222 kg/ha more than those beside open grazing areas in the drought-affected 2023 season, and a panel estimate put the grain advantage at 586.6 kg/ha [ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_1, ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_2].
conditionality: Most units are WOCAT compiler ratings, and one Ethiopian compiler rates crop production as unchanged; much of the evidence is fodder, a component of the production gap rather than crop yield. The Brazilian quasi-experimental gains apply to the poorest quarter of municipalities in an upper-middle-income state, and the source reports a heterogeneous, negative response in better-off municipalities. The Tigray advantage was concentrated in the drier year: no statistically significant yield difference was found in the second production year (2024/2025), and it concerns downstream cropland compared with open grazing [ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_3, ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_4].

effect_mechanism: Restoration reaches poverty mainly through income from forest products, payments and employment. Restored forests contribute to diversified livelihoods and higher income from timber and non-timber products, naturally regenerating forests supply both, and secondary forest regeneration combined with palm-fruit harvest in Brazil's Atlantic forest improved farmer income [ev_household_income_iufro20_8, ev_household_income_chazdon16_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_10]. Community forest management in Nepal reduced both poverty and deforestation in an analysis of 18,000 community forests, 68% of community forestry cases reporting livelihood outcomes showed income increases, community forestry in Madagascar had a small but positive impact on living standards, and in Mexico's Sierra Norte de Puebla community forestry provides year-round wage labour and a profit share of 10 to 20 thousand pesos per member after harvest [ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_2, ev_household_income_iufro20_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_2, ev_household_income_ceballos21_1]. In China, the Sloping Land Conversion Program increased local incomes in Wuqi County by 164 percent and off-farm income by 20 times, and afforestation subsidies raised off-farm labour earnings [ev_household_income_wri17_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_9]; in Costa Rica, payments for reforestation made up 18.66% of participants' income, against about 10% of family income in other Latin American programmes [ev_household_income_padilla17_1, ev_household_income_padilla17_2]. Mangrove planting in Viet Nam raised shell and oyster yields per hectare, with benefit-cost ratios of 3.06 to 68.92 excluding ecological benefits, and a global meta-analysis gives mangrove restoration benefit-cost ratios of 10.50 to 6.83 [ev_household_income_ifrc11_1, ev_economic_return_ifrc11_1, ev_economic_return_su21_1]. Global modelling gives benefit-cost ratios of $7.5 to $30.9 for restoring 350 million hectares of degraded forest land and about $2 to $32 across forest biomes, and plantations would be profitable without carbon payments across 28.3% of the plantation-feasible area [ev_economic_return_wri17_1, ev_economic_return_wri17_2, ev_economic_return_busch24_1]. Protected areas contributed to poverty alleviation in Costa Rica and Thailand, and households near GEF forest-management sites in Uganda show positive income effects [ev_rural_poverty_puri16_1, ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_1, ev_household_income_gefieo19_1]. WOCAT compilers across Africa, Asia, Central Asia and Latin America mostly rate long-term returns as positive or very positive and food self-sufficiency or production risk as improved; the Niger compiler estimates that assisted natural regeneration raises food security by 20% at least, and the Indian compiler cites more fodder and water [ev_economic_return_wocat_1048_2011_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_1577_2013_costbenefit_maintenance_long, ev_food_security_wocat_2325_2017_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_food_security_wocat_5243_2019_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_household_income_wocat_1048_2011_farm_income, ev_household_income_wocat_1533_2011_farm_income]. A World Bank study for coastal Bangladesh models livelihood benefits of mangrove restoration at 3,700 to 86,000 USD per hectare [ev_economic_return_wbmang25_1].
conditionality: Negative and null findings are substantial. Reforestation projects have often deprived people of food production and forest-product collection without viable alternatives, and restoration can reduce on-farm income by taking agricultural land [ev_household_income_le12_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_7]; the Turkmen compiler expects annual income to fall by 20 - 25% for the first 1-2 years, the Tunisian compiler rates farm income as reduced, the Ugandan compiler rates it unchanged, and the Cabo Verde compiler rates food security unchanged because the practice reduces land-use options [ev_household_income_wocat_1529_2012_farm_income, ev_household_income_wocat_1568_2013_farm_income, ev_household_income_wocat_1577_2013_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_1523_2011_food_security_selfsufficiency]. In south-west Madagascar conservation-oriented community management contracts were not profitable and the Gelose transfers did not raise community incomes [ev_economic_return_ramamo12_1, ev_household_income_ramamo12_1]; REDD+ contributions in Nepal were nominal, from 3.2% of the poorest households' income to 0.3% for the less poor, other REDD+ studies found no effect or potentially negative effects in Indonesia, and payment programmes have either a small positive or neutral effect on poverty [ev_household_income_iufro20_4, ev_household_income_iufro20_5, ev_household_income_iufro20_6, ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_3]. Brazil's Reflorestar programme showed no statistically significant effect on municipal GDP or employment, the GEF forest-management portfolio returns a benefit-cost ratio of 0.69 counting carbon only, and in Nepal benefits of community forestry go mostly to better-off households while poor households bear more of the costs [ev_economic_return_seixas24_1, ev_economic_return_gefieo19_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_3]. Few studies have substantiated that services of restored forests alleviate poverty, and where they do it takes years or decades [ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_4]. Much of the positive evidence is WOCAT compiler ratings, an implementer-commissioned evaluation in Viet Nam, carbon valuations rather than cash (such as $411–1,236 per hectare a year for forest conservation in Colombia), perception scores (the Costa Rica economic impact of 63.9%), secondary citations, or subsidy-driven gains without a counterfactual (Wuqi) [ev_economic_return_ifrc11_2, ev_economic_return_wri17_3, ev_household_income_padilla17_3, ev_household_income_wri17_1], and protected areas, REDD+ and payment schemes are conservation instruments rather than restoration practices. The Bangladesh figures are modelled present values transferred from a global valuation meta-regression and come from grey literature [ev_economic_return_wbmang25_1].

A World Bank study for coastal Bangladesh models livelihood benefits of mangrove restoration at 3,700 to 86,000 USD/ha, with regional means of 22,039 to 30,330 USD/ha [ev_economic_return_wbmang25_1].
conditionality: The Viet Nam figures come from an evaluation commissioned by the implementer, model benefits forward and include ecological benefits the source says had yet to materialise; the meta-analysis pools unpaired benefit and cost samples. Poverty is reached only through proxies (economic return, food security, income), and the WOCAT entries are compiler ratings. The Bangladesh figures are modelled present values transferred from a global valuation meta-regression, not observed household income, and come from grey literature [ev_economic_return_wbmang25_1].

effect_mechanism: Tree cover reduces erosion by protecting the soil surface, slowing runoff and holding slopes. In the Potwar Upland of Pakistan runoff and sedimentation from sheet erosion fell 55 percent and 78 percent five years after tree planting and closure of slopes to grazing [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_5, ev_runoff_reduction_forbes11_1]; in Ethiopia, a meta-analysis finds areas closed to grazing and agriculture had runoff coefficients of 4% against 19% on control sites, and tree planting on degraded catchments cut annual runoff from 242 to 148 mm/year [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_1, ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_2]. Targeted reforestation of 9.3 percent of New Zealand's Waipaoa catchment is modelled to decrease landslide sediment inputs by about 20 percent, tree planting on susceptible slopes can reduce landslide risk, eucalyptus afforestation plots in Calabria, Italy with good canopy gave lower sediment concentrations than plots with little or no tree cover, and China's reforestation programmes reduced soil erosion and sediments [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_6, ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_1, ev_erosion_hazard_porto09_1, ev_erosion_hazard_iufro18_1].
